metadata.title: Internal Enterprise Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how an internal enterprise platform would need to change when AI agents become legally accountable actors, an acquisition brings conflicting identities and operating definitions, sanctions force a country exit, or an acquired operation must be separated while automated work continues.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: Employees enter through one corporate identity, work is routed through shared workflows and approvals, AI assistants automate steps, source systems feed common metrics, and finance, risk, managers, and executives see consolidated outcomes. The design assumes one enterprise boundary, stable identity and role meaning, compatible metrics, and automation that acts only as an extension of a known employee.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The changed design separates person, employment, legal entity, country, role, identity, device, entitlement, delegated authority, workflow instance, policy, AI agent, model, evidence, proposed action, human decision, execution, metric definition, source assertion, record obligation, and organizational transition. This lets acquired operating models coexist while they are reconciled, makes automated actions explainable and reversible, and closes or transfers a country operation without losing work, controls, or people obligations.
metadata.note: These tests attack the assumption that an enterprise has one stable identity, policy, metric, and automation context. The explicit change is to version who may act, for which organization and purpose, using which evidence, under which policy, and during which organizational state.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: New workplace law makes every consequential AI-agent action explainable, contestable, and human-owned
stressors.detection: Final law and guidance, inventory of agents and automated workflows, model and prompt versions, delegated permissions, affected employees and customers, approvals, executed actions, incidents, complaints, audit requests, and human ownership records.
stressors.attractor: AI agents approve spend, change access, route candidates, update forecasts, message customers, and resolve cases, but the enterprise cannot consistently show whose authority they used, which evidence shaped an action, which policy applied, or how a person can stop and contest the outcome. Disabling all automation stalls operations; leaving it opaque creates legal and trust failure.
stressors.businessReaction: Classify consequential actions, assign accountable owners, constrain each agent's purpose and authority, preserve decision evidence, require human review at defined boundaries, notify affected people, provide correction and appeal, reverse unsafe actions, monitor drift, and retire agents whose controls no longer hold.
stressors.residue: Separate business intent, requester, affected party, agent, model and prompt version, tool, delegated authority, data purpose, evidence, policy version, proposed action, confidence, human review, approval, execution, downstream effect, notification, contest, reversal, and outcome. Authority applies to one action class and expires when material context changes.

impacts.effect: Enterprise automation scales only when each agent action has bounded authority, evidence, accountability, and recovery.
Platform administrators can automate cross-system work without turning agent autonomy into invisible organizational authority.
Controls evaluate purpose, authority, evidence, affected party, consequence, human review, contest, and reversal before execution.
Audit evidence completeness follows the complete proposal-to-execution-and-reversal chain for automated actions.
Adds agent registration, scoped delegation, action simulation, review gates, explanations, appeals, monitoring, and rollback.
Makes accountable action and recovery part of the automation path rather than a later audit exercise.
Versions agent, model, prompt, tools, purpose, delegated authority, policy, evaluation, and runtime action evidence.
Designs explicit human, agent, review, contest, compensation, and recovery steps into reusable workflows.
Evaluates approval rights and required review against the current actor, action, consequence, organization, and policy.
Owns agent accountability with business owners, employee representatives, legal, security, risk, data, platform, and support teams.
Makes governed enterprise-agent action and contestability a workplace-platform benchmark.

stressors.name: An acquisition doubles the workforce but brings incompatible identities, workflows, and operating metrics
stressors.detection: Deal close and integration perimeter, legal entities and employee rosters, identity providers, source systems, role and approval models, workflow inventories, metric definitions, contracts, duplicate vendors, operational reports, and integration milestones.
stressors.attractor: The same customer, employee, revenue stage, cost center, control, and service request mean different things in each company. Prematurely forcing one model breaks local operations and produces misleading executive totals; leaving everything separate prevents shared service, risk, and investment decisions.
stressors.businessReaction: Preserve both operating models, link equivalent and disputed concepts, establish people and organization identity, select decision-critical integrations, route work across both environments, expose reconciliation gaps, retire duplicate tools deliberately, and move toward shared definitions through owned milestones.
stressors.residue: Separate person from employment and source identity; legal entity from operating unit; real-world customer or vendor from source account; metric concept from local definition and observation; workflow intent from local implementation; and system from business capability. Mappings, confidence, owner, effective time, conflicts, and migration state remain visible.

impacts.effect: Executives gain one operating view without pretending incompatible definitions and systems already agree.
Leadership can run the combined enterprise from reconciled evidence with local meaning and uncertainty intact.
Normalization shows source definition, mappings, exclusions, comparability, ownership, effective date, and unresolved conflict.
Time to integrate a business unit measures decision-ready identity, workflow, metric, control, and service coverage.
Adds federated intake, cross-company routing, semantic mappings, transition state, and shared-service migration.
Builds a governed combined view from linked source assertions instead of overwriting local operating facts.
Links people, employments, identities, managers, organizations, roles, and effective transitions across both companies.
Maps shared concepts to local definitions and preserves ownership, confidence, conflict, and decision fitness.
Catalogs duplicate systems and workflows with capabilities, users, dependencies, cost, risk, and migration decisions.
Owns semantic integration with acquired business owners, HR, finance, commercial, service, platform, risk, and data teams.
Makes federated post-acquisition service and operating-model integration an enterprise-platform benchmark.

stressors.name: Sanctions require the enterprise to stop operating in one country within seventy-two hours
stressors.detection: Government and legal notices, affected legal entities, employees and contractors, customers and vendors, work queues, bank and payroll routes, identities and devices, data locations, contracts, approvals, records and legal holds, facilities, and service dependencies.
stressors.attractor: Access, payment, employment, customer service, data handling, contracts, and approvals that were valid yesterday may become prohibited or impossible at different times. A blanket identity shutdown abandons people, work, evidence, and customer obligations; leaving access unchanged violates sanctions and exposes the enterprise.
stressors.businessReaction: Interpret prohibited and permitted activity, identify affected people and work, protect employees, suspend restricted transactions, transfer essential duties, revoke or narrow access, secure devices and records, preserve legal holds, communicate with customers and vendors, handle payroll or benefits lawfully, and document every exception and closure.
stressors.residue: Separate person, employment, legal entity, country, residency, role, identity, device, entitlement, business duty, case or task, delegation, approval, customer or vendor obligation, payment route, record, legal hold, restriction, exception, transition, and closure evidence. Each right and obligation can change independently with an effective time.

impacts.effect: Employees receive clear, humane work and access transitions when geopolitical rules abruptly change their operating context.
Administrators can change identity, device, and access state without losing employment, work, record, or legal context.
Detection combines legal entity, geography, employment, duties, restrictions, effective dates, and required transition actions.
Recovery time measures safe transfer or closure of work and obligations, not only restoration of an automation.
Adds country-exit work guidance, delegated queues, employee communications, support, record handling, and status.
Coordinates access restriction, duty transfer, records, customer and vendor obligations, exceptions, and closure.
Executes scoped device and access transitions with effective dates, exceptions, confirmation, and recovery state.
Separates organizational role, business duty, system entitlement, geography, legal restriction, and delegated authority.
Preserves required records and legal holds while applying locality, access, transfer, and deletion decisions.
Owns technical and work continuity with HR, legal, sanctions, finance, security, service, workplace, and business leaders.
Makes jurisdiction-aware workforce and access transition a global enterprise-operations benchmark.

stressors.name: The acquired operation is in the sanctioned country and must be separated while AI agents still hold active authority
stressors.detection: Acquisition and country-exit perimeters, people and identity links, source semantic mappings, active workflows and agents, delegated authorities, affected tasks and transactions, policy and sanctions scope, records, controls, legal holds, customers, vendors, and transition deadlines.
stressors.attractor: The enterprise cannot reliably tell which acquired identities, metrics, work, records, and agent actions belong to the restricted operation. Immediately disabling everything may abandon lawful obligations; allowing automated workflows to continue may execute prohibited payments, access changes, or customer actions under ambiguous authority.
stressors.businessReaction: Freeze high-consequence agent actions, establish the legal and operating perimeter, reconcile decision-critical identities and work, revoke or transfer delegated authority, route permitted obligations to accountable owners, suspend prohibited transactions, preserve records and evidence, support affected people, and prove separation completion.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: scoped agent authority stops ambiguous automation, federated identity and semantics reveal the acquired operating context, and effective-dated country-exit records transfer or close access, work, payments, and evidence. One governed separation case composes the existing parts.

impacts.effect: Finance, legal, compliance, and security leaders can prove that prohibited actions stopped and lawful obligations remained controlled.
Policy enforcement follows the actual entity, person, authority, action, record, and transition rather than a coarse account block.
The control view distinguishes frozen agents, transferred work, restricted payments, retained records, exceptions, and completion evidence.
Evidence completeness covers the full separation perimeter and every automated or human action taken during it.
Composes financial exposure, transaction suspension, obligations, approvals, exceptions, record evidence, and final control sign-off.
Reuses agent, semantic-integration, and country-exit residues to prove the separation without reconstructing it manually.
Links every relevant control to source facts, agent and human actions, exceptions, evidence, and outcomes.
Routes permitted exceptions with authority, scope, compensating controls, owner, expiry, and closure.
Shows executives the separation perimeter, material exposure, people impact, unresolved decisions, and readiness.
Coordinates the separation across legal, sanctions, finance, HR, security, data, automation, operations, and executive teams.
Makes governed post-acquisition geopolitical separation a full-enterprise-platform benchmark.
